characterization_methods.key_findings: For the 1050 °C condition, austenite (FCC) and ferrite (BCC) peaks are present while the carbide markers are absent (Cr7C3 and κ-carbides dissolved at 1050 °C); the measured ferrite fraction for DP1050-1 is not reported ('-') in Table 1.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Diffraction angle 2θ 35–80°; annealed specimens at 600–1050 °C (5 min) in Fig. 1a
characterization_methods.purpose: To identify phase constituents (austenite FCC, ferrite BCC, β-Mn, carbides) and to determine the ferrite fraction of the annealed structures.

characterization_methods.key_findings: DP1050-1 (f1/f2) shows dispersed small red α ferrite regions and thin/discontinuous δ ferrite bands in a fully recrystallized austenite matrix (uniform yellow GROD) with annealing twins; quantified α = 2.7%, δ = 4.6%, Rex-γ fraction = 96.8%.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Phase (PH) maps and grain-reference-orientation-deviation (GROD) maps of austenite; dark lines in austenite are high-angle grain boundaries with misorientation >15°; 20 µm scale bar
characterization_methods.purpose: To quantify recrystallized austenite fraction (GROD < 2°), α and δ ferrite fractions and to examine phase distribution and annealing twins.

characterization_methods.key_findings: Cr7C3 carbides (DP950-5) and intragranular κ-carbide nanoparticles (DP1000-5) were identified in other samples; for the 1050 °C annealing, carbides disappear/dissolve, consistent with the XRD result.
characterization_methods.purpose: To identify carbides and κ-carbide nanoparticles in the annealed duplex structure.

characterization_methods.key_findings: Ferrite is clearly softer than the recrystallized austenite (measured on DP1000-5 in Fig. S4), explaining lower YS in the softer-ferrite specimens.
characterization_methods.purpose: To study the mechanical response of different microstructural constituents (ferrite vs. recrystallized austenite).

characterization_methods.key_findings: DP1050-1: YS 905 ± 15 MPa, UTS 1205 ± 10 MPa, TE 47.5 ± 1.0 %; highest TE but lowest YS/UTS among annealed specimens.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Strain rate 10^-3 s^-1, room temperature, flat dog-bone specimens with 25 mm gage length along RD
characterization_methods.purpose: To measure YS, UTS, TE and specific strength of the annealed specimens including DP1050-1.

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Cracks are easily initiated at the α/γ interfaces during deformation, because the granular α ferrite grains at boundaries/triple points act as nucleation sites; however these cracks can be captured and deflected by δ ferrite bands where they even get blunted. In the duplex design the granular α ferrite grains restrain austenite grain growth when sufficient.

defect_interactions.interaction_type: crack capture and deflection by δ ferrite bands
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: δ ferrite bands capture and deflect propagating cracks; cracks may propagate into the soft δ ferrite bands and get blunted through dislocation emission and local plastic dissipation near the crack tip, delocalizing plastic strain.

interfaces.interface_notes: The described crack-nucleation/deflection mechanisms are the general ductility mechanism of the developed duplex design summarized for the whole study; quantitative crack analysis was performed on DP1000-5/DP1000-5-TD (Fig. 4) rather than specifically on DP1050-1.
interfaces.phase_evolution: At 1050 °C the ferrite fraction is reduced with ferrite-to-austenite transformation; Cr7C3 carbides and the intergranular κ-carbides significantly dissolve/disappear at 1050 °C, so the annealed structure is essentially a fully recrystallized austenite matrix with residual α and δ ferrite.

comparative_performance.comparison_description: DP1050-1 (with DP1000-5) exhibits a product of SUTS and TE exceeding 8 GPa·g⁻¹·cm³·%, clearly superior to existing high-strength metallic materials: less than 4 GPa·g⁻¹·cm³·% for 2000 series aerospace aluminum alloys and Ti6Al4V, and in the ranges 2.7–6.5 and 2.9–7.4 GPa·g⁻¹·cm³·% for duplex and austenitic Fe-Mn-Al-C steels respectively. DP1050-1 lies beyond the 8 GPa·g⁻¹·cm³·% contour in the SUTS–TE comparison plot (Fig. 3b).
comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Product of SUTS and TE (specific ultimate tensile strength × total elongation)

processing_steps.method: vacuum induction melting and casting into ingot
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Melted in a vacuum induction furnace under argon atmosphere and cast into ingot.
Homogenization of the ingot at 1200 °C for 2 h before forging/hot rolling.
Ingot forged to a thick slab.
HR plates heated to 1050 °C and isothermally held for 0.5 h, then quenched in water.
The defining annealing for DP1050-1: CR sheet annealed at 1050 °C for 1 min and then quenched in water again.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Uniaxial tensile tests; three measurements made for each heat treatment condition and averaged.
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: Flat dog-bone-shaped tensile specimen with a gage length of 25 mm, length direction along the rolling direction (RD)

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress-strain curve of DP1050-1 (purple) in Fig. 3a extends past 40% strain at lower plateau stresses compared with DP1000-5.

phases_present.morphology: fully recrystallized austenite matrix containing annealing twins
granular, dispersed small red ferrite regions within the austenite matrix
banded, elongated along the rolling direction; bands thinner and more discontinuous than lower-temperature specimens

microstructure_list.region: overall (RD–ND plane), EBSD phase/GROD map f1/f2 in Fig. 2

structures.overall_structure: Austenite-ferrite duplex microstructure obtained by annealing the cold rolled structure at 1050 °C for 1 min, showing complete recrystallization of austenite (Rex-γ fraction 96.8%) and reduced ferrite fraction. The microstructure comprises a fully recrystallized austenite matrix with annealing twins, dispersed small granular α ferrite regions and δ ferrite bands that are thinner and more discontinuous than at lower annealing temperatures.

unmapped_findings: DP1050-1 specific strength values (Table 1): SYS = 142.3 ± 2.4 MPa·g⁻¹·cm³ and SUTS = 189.5 ± 1.6 MPa·g⁻¹·cm³ (these are the lowest specific strength values among the annealed specimens but the highest TE).
For DP1050-1 the ferrite fraction measured by XRD is not reported ('-') in Table 1, in contrast to the EBSD-based α (2.7%) and δ (4.6%) fractions.

Increasing the annealing temperature to 1050 °C causes TE to improve but YS/UTS to be remarkably impaired, primarily because of austenite grain growth (9.65 ± 8.17 μm) and the significant dissolution of Cr7C3 carbides/the intergranular κ-carbides (b0025, b0015).
The alloy measured ultralow density of 6.36 g·cm^-3 was obtained by buoyancy balance according to Archimedes Principle (b0012), shared by all annealed specimens including DP1050-1.
